repositories.name: t3code
repositories.readme:
# T3 Code

T3 Code is an "agent harness control surface". It enables control of the agents on your machine with a best-in-class mobile app ([iOS](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/t3-code-remote-claude-more/id6787819824), [Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.t3tools.t3code)), [web app](https://app.t3.codes) and [Electron-based desktop app](https://t3.codes).

Works with your subscriptions on Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, and fx. If they're set up on your computer, T3 Code can control them.

## "Wait, what are you selling me?"

Nothing. We built T3 Code because we wanted the best possible development experience with agents. We were inspired by existing solutions like the Codex desktop app, Conductor, Claude Desktop and Cursor Glass, but none met our bar.

We wanted something performant, remote-ready, and truly open. If we ever go the wrong direction, we want you to have everything you need to fork and build the editor that you want.

## Installation

> [!WARNING]
> T3 Code currently supports Codex, Claude, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Antigravity, and fx. Install and authenticate at least one provider before use:
>
> - Codex: install [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/cli) and run `codex login`
> - Claude: install [Claude Code](https://claude.com/product/claude-code) and run `claude auth login`
> - Cursor: install [Cursor CLI](https://cursor.com/cli) and run `agent login`
> - Grok Build: install [Grok Build CLI](https://x.ai/cli) and run `grok login`
> - OpenCode: install [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) and run `opencode auth login`
> - Antigravity: enable it in Settings, then use **Install Antigravity** and **Sign in with Google**. No CLI is required.
> - fx: install [fx](https://fx.sh) and run `fx login` on the machine running the T3 Code server ([setup guide](./docs/user/providers-fx.md))

### Command line

```bash
curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh
```

On Windows, in PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://t3.codes/install.ps1 | iex
```

Then run `t3` to start the server and open the local web app. `t3 service install` keeps it running in the background, `t3 update` moves to a newer release, and `t3 --help` has the full reference.

To try it once without installing, run `npx t3@latest` instead.

### Desktop app

Install the latest version of the desktop app from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases), or from your favorite package registry:

#### Windows (`winget`)

```bash
winget install T3Tools.T3Code
```

#### Windows (`scoop`)

```bash
scoop install extras/t3code
```

#### macOS (Homebrew)

```bash
brew install --cask t3-code
```

#### Debian, Ubuntu (`.deb`)

Download the `.deb` from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/releases), then:

```bash
sudo apt install ./T3-Code-*.deb
```

#### Arch Linux (AUR)

Stable:

```bash
yay -S t3code-bin
```

Nightly:

```bash
yay -S t3code-nightly-bin
```

The AUR packaging is maintained in this repository under [`packaging/aur`](./packaging/aur).

#### Nix (nixpkgs)

```bash
nix profile add github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-unstable#t3code
```

The package is maintained in [nixpkgs](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/tree/nixos-unstable/pkgs/by-name/t3/t3code)
and includes the desktop app (`t3code-desktop`) and the `t3` command.
See [Nix installation](./docs/user/install.md#nix-nixpkgs) for NixOS configuration and updates.

## Some notes

We are very very early in this project. Expect bugs.

We are (mostly) not accepting contributions yet. Small fixes may be considered. Big features will not be.

## Documentation

Full docs live in [docs/](./docs). There's no docs site yet.

- [FAQ](./docs/user/faq.md)
- [Install and first run](./docs/user/install.md)
- [Permission modes](./docs/user/permission-modes.md)
- [Keyboard shortcuts](./docs/user/keybindings.md)
- [Project settings](./docs/user/project-settings.md)
- [Appearance preferences](./docs/user/appearance.md)
- [Remote access from a phone or another machine](./docs/user/remote-access.md)
- [Connect Claude Code, Codex, ChatGPT and other agents over MCP](./docs/user/outside-agents.md)
- [Keeping app and server in sync](./docs/user/updating.md)
- [Source control integrations](./docs/user/source-control.md)
- Multiple accounts: [Codex](./docs/user/providers-codex.md) · [Claude](./docs/user/providers-claude.md)
- [Run T3 Code as a background service](./docs/user/background-service.md)

Building from source? Start at [docs/internals/overview.md](./docs/internals/overview.md).

## If you REALLY want to contribute still.... read this first

### Install `vp`

T3 Code uses Vite+ so you'll need to install the global `vp` command-line tool.

#### macOS / Linux

```bash
curl -fsSL https://vite.plus | bash
```

#### Windows

```bash
irm https://vite.plus/ps1 | iex
```

Checkout their getting started guide for more information: https://viteplus.dev/guide/

### Install dependencies

```bash
vp i
```

Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md) before reporting a bug or opening a PR.

Have a feature request? Start an [Ideas discussion](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/discussions/categories/ideas).

Need support? Join the [Discord](https://discord.gg/jn4EGJjrvv).

🇨🇳 中文 • 🇹🇼 繁體中文 • 🇯🇵 日本語 • 🇵🇹 Português • 🇧🇷 Português • 🇰🇷 한국어 • 🇪🇸 Español • 🇩🇪 Deutsch • 🇫🇷 Français • 🇮🇱 עברית • 🇸🇦 العربية • 🇷🇺 Русский • 🇵🇱 Polski • 🇨🇿 Čeština • 🇳🇱 Nederlands • 🇹🇷 Türkçe • 🇺🇦 Українська • 🇻🇳 Tiếng Việt • 🇵🇭 Tagalog • 🇮🇩 Indonesia • 🇹🇭 ไทย • 🇮🇳 हिन्दी • 🇧🇩 বাংলা • 🇵🇰 اردو • 🇷🇴 Română • 🇸🇪 Svenska • 🇮🇹 Italiano • 🇬🇷 Ελληνικά • 🇭🇺 Magyar • 🇫🇮 Suomi • 🇩🇰 Dansk • 🇳🇴 Norsk

Persistent memory compression system built for Claude Code.


Quick Start • How It Works • Search Tools • Documentation • Configuration • Troubleshooting • License

Claude-Mem seamlessly preserves context across sessions by automatically capturing tool usage observations, generating semantic summaries, and making them available to future sessions. This enables Claude to maintain continuity of knowledge about projects even after sessions end or reconnect.

--- ## Quick Start Install claude-mem for Grok Bot: ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide grok-bot ``` Grok Bot has no host hooks, so we watch the chat log files. Default is CMEM Pro, the hosted memory. Local observer is opt-in: `--provider host`. Installing this plugin does not install Cursor. **Awareness push pilot (LFG + Orifice):** needle observations (`decision`, `bugfix`, `security_alert`, `sensitive`) are appended as dated `- YYYY-MM-DD [awareness] …` lines into that bot's `memory/log/YYYY-MM.md`. Grok Bot already re-reads the log from disk. This does not write `profile.md`, user-memory, or project memory. Disable with `CLAUDE_MEM_GROK_BOT_AWARENESS_ENABLED=false`. Install with a single command: ```bash npx claude-mem install ``` The installer sets everything up first, then asks you to sign in to claude-mem in your browser (email magic link — no card required). Signing in provisions a memory key for your account and unlocks the **claude-mem observer** with a **30 Day Free Trial**: memory runs off-plan, so you get up to 100% more usage from your plan. When the free trial ends, memory automatically falls back to your Anthropic plan unless you subscribe. After sign-in you pick your memory provider — the claude-mem observer, your own OpenRouter or Gemini key, or your Anthropic plan. Prefer to skip the sign-in? Pass an explicit `--provider` flag, set `CLAUDE_MEM_ONLINE_OPTIN=false`, or run in CI/non-interactive shells — the installer completes without any account interaction. Or install for OpenCode: ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide opencode ``` This works with OpenCode 1.3.4 or later, including OpenCode 2. Restart OpenCode after installing. Or install for **T3 Code** (Codex and Claude Code providers): ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide t3code ``` The installer discovers T3 Code's enabled providers, registers native Claude-Mem plugins in their configured homes, and supports T3-managed Codex. Restart T3 Code, trust the provider's hooks when prompted, and start a new thread. See the [T3 Code integration guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/t3code-integration) for custom server settings, status, and removal. Or install for Antigravity CLI ([setup guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/antigravity-cli/setup)): ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide antigravity ``` Or install for OMP (Oh My Pi): ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide omp ``` Or install the native Pi extension or DeepSeek Harness plugin: ```bash npx claude-mem install --ide pi npx claude-mem install --ide dsh --dsh-profile tui ``` Pi and DeepSeek Harness use the worker runtime. See [native harness setup](docs/native-harness-integrations.md) for capture, recall, and troubleshooting. Or install from the plugin marketplace inside Claude Code: ```bash /plugin marketplace add thedotmack/claude-mem /plugin install claude-mem ``` Restart Claude Code. Context from previous sessions will automatically appear in new sessions. > **Note:** Claude-Mem is also published on npm, but `npm install -g claude-mem` installs the **SDK/library only** — it does not register the plugin hooks or set up the worker service. Always install via `npx claude-mem install` or the `/plugin` commands above. ### 🦞 OpenClaw Gateway Install claude-mem as a persistent memory plugin on [OpenClaw](https://openclaw.ai) gateways with a single command: ```bash curl -fsSL https://install.cmem.ai/openclaw.sh | bash ``` The installer handles dependencies, plugin setup, AI provider configuration, worker startup, and optional real-time observation feeds to Telegram, Discord, Slack, and more. See the [OpenClaw Integration Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/openclaw-integration) for details. **Key Features:** - 🧠 **Persistent Memory** - Context survives across sessions - 📊 **Progressive Disclosure** - Layered memory retrieval with token cost visibility - 🔍 **Smart Search (Default)** - Query your project history with the three-step mem-search skill - 🖥️ **Local My Work** - Live requests, progress, human handoffs and a saved review queue at the worker URL printed on startup. [Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/my-work). Memory, sessions and settings remain at `/viewer`. - 👥 **TeamBrain** - An optional shared workspace beside My Work, with real team work lists, member attribution and linked findings. Each person chooses what to share; personal requests and review notes stay separate. [Set up a team](https://cmem.ai/teambrain/start). - 💻 **Claude Desktop Skill** - Search memory from Claude Desktop conversations - 🔒 **Privacy Control** - Use `` tags to exclude sensitive content from storage - 🖼️ **Screenshots (opt-in, off by default)** - Keep converted copies of tool screenshots under `~/.claude-mem/media-v1/`, upload them to cmem.ai only when Cloud Sync is on, and send them to the observer model only when image inference is separately enabled ([details](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/configuration#screenshots-and-images-opt-in)) - ⚙️ **Context Configuration** - Fine-grained control over what context gets injected - 🤖 **Automatic Operation** - No manual intervention required - 🔗 **Citations** - Reference past observations with IDs through the worker API or view all in the web viewer --- ## Documentation 📚 **[View Full Documentation](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/)** - Browse on official website ### Getting Started - **[Installation Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/installation)** - Quick start & advanced installation - **[Usage Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/getting-started)** - How Claude-Mem works automatically - **[Search Tools](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/search-tools)** - Query your project history with natural language - **[Cloud Sync](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/cloud-sync)** - Back up your memories to cmem.ai — no daemon, the worker syncs on write ### Best Practices - **[Context Engineering](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/context-engineering)** - AI agent context optimization principles - **[Progressive Disclosure](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/progressive-disclosure)** - Philosophy behind Claude-Mem's context priming strategy ### Architecture - **[Overview](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/overview)** - System components & data flow - **[Architecture Evolution](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture-evolution)** - The journey from v3 to v5 - **[Hooks Architecture](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/hooks-architecture)** - How Claude-Mem uses lifecycle hooks - **[Hooks Reference](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/hooks)** - Every hook entry explained - **[Worker Service](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/worker-service)** - HTTP API & Bun management - **[Database](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/database)** - SQLite schema & FTS5 search - **[Search Architecture](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/search-architecture)** - Hybrid search with Chroma vector database ### Configuration & Development - **[Configuration](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/configuration)** - Environment variables & settings - **[Development](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/development)** - Building, testing, contributing - **[Troubleshooting](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/troubleshooting)** - Common issues & solutions --- ## How It Works **Core Components:** 1. **Lifecycle Hooks** - SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd. Each is one shell-free command, `claude-mem hook claude-code `, run by a small launcher that the installer puts on PATH 2. **Smart Install** - Cached dependency checker (Setup hook on `claude --init` / `--maintenance`, plus `npx claude-mem install` / `repair`) 3. **Worker Service** - Local HTTP API with web viewer UI and search endpoints, managed by Bun 4. **SQLite Database** - Stores sessions, observations, summaries 5. **mem-search Skill** - Natural language queries with progressive disclosure 6. **Chroma Vector Database** - Hybrid semantic + keyword search for intelligent context retrieval See [Architecture Overview](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/architecture/overview) for details. --- ## MCP Search Tools Claude-Mem provides intelligent memory search through **4 MCP tools** following a token-efficient **3-layer workflow pattern**: **The 3-Layer Workflow:** 1. **`search`** - Get compact index with IDs (~50-100 tokens/result) 2. **`timeline`** - Get chronological context around interesting results 3. **`get_observations`** - Fetch full details ONLY for filtered IDs (~500-1,000 tokens/result) **How It Works:** - Claude uses MCP tools to search your memory - Start with `search` to get an index of results - Use `timeline` to see what was happening around specific observations - Use `get_observations` to fetch full details for relevant IDs - **~10x token savings** by filtering before fetching details **Available MCP Tools:** 1. **`search`** - Search memory index with full-text queries, filters by type/date/project 2. **`timeline`** - Get chronological context around a specific observation or query 3. **`get_observations`** - Fetch full observation details by IDs (always batch multiple IDs) **Example Usage:** ```typescript // Step 1: Search for index search(query="authentication bug", type="bugfix", limit=10) // Step 2: Review index, identify relevant IDs (e.g., #123, #456) // Step 3: Fetch full details get_observations(ids=[123, 456]) ``` See [Search Tools Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/usage/search-tools) for detailed examples. --- ## System Requirements - **Node.js**: 20.0.0 or higher - **Claude Code**: Latest version with plugin support - **Bun**: JavaScript runtime and process manager (auto-installed if missing) - **uv**: Python package manager for vector search (auto-installed if missing) - **SQLite 3**: For persistent storage (bundled) --- ### Windows Setup Notes If you see an error like: ```powershell npm : The term 'npm' is not recognized as the name of a cmdlet ``` Make sure Node.js and npm are installed and added to your PATH. Download the latest Node.js installer from https://nodejs.org and restart your terminal after installation. Claude Code hooks do not need Git Bash. Each hook runs `claude-mem` directly, and `npx claude-mem install` places that launcher at `%LOCALAPPDATA%\claude-mem\bin\claude-mem.exe` and adds the folder to your user Path. Restart your terminal or IDE afterwards so Claude Code picks up the new Path. If hooks report `Executable not found in $PATH: "claude-mem"`, run `npx claude-mem doctor` and see [Troubleshooting](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/troubleshooting#claude-mem-command-not-found-in-hooks). --- ## Configuration Settings are managed in `~/.claude-mem/settings.json` (auto-created with defaults on first run). Configure AI model, worker port, data directory, log level, and context injection settings. To include observations from every harness in Claude Code and Codex SessionStart context, set `"CLAUDE_MEM_SESSION_START_INCLUDE_ALL_SOURCES": "true"` in that file, or enable **Include all sources at session start** in the viewer settings. The default is `"false"`, which limits startup context to the current harness. The observation count limit still applies across the selected sources. See the **[Configuration Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/configuration)** for all available settings and examples. ### Mode & Language Configuration Claude-Mem supports multiple workflow modes and languages via the `CLAUDE_MEM_MODE` setting. This option controls both: - The workflow behavior (e.g. code, chill, investigation) - The language used in generated observations #### How to Configure Edit your settings file at `~/.claude-mem/settings.json`: ```json { "CLAUDE_MEM_MODE": "code--zh" } ``` Modes are defined in `plugin/modes/`. To see all available modes locally: ```bash ls ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/thedotmack/plugin/modes/ ``` #### Available Modes | Mode | Description | |------------|-------------------------| | `code` | Default English mode | | `code--zh` | Simplified Chinese mode | | `code--ja` | Japanese mode | Language-specific modes follow the pattern `code--[lang]` where `[lang]` is the ISO 639-1 language code (e.g., `zh` for Chinese, `ja` for Japanese, `es` for Spanish). > Note: `code--zh` (Simplified Chinese) is already built-in — no additional installation or plugin update is required. #### After Changing Mode Restart Claude Code to apply the new mode configuration. --- ## Development See the **[Development Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/development)** for build instructions, testing, and contribution workflow. --- ## Troubleshooting If experiencing issues, describe the problem to Claude and the troubleshoot skill will automatically diagnose and provide fixes. See the **[Troubleshooting Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/troubleshooting)** for common issues and solutions. --- ## Bug Reports Create comprehensive bug reports with the automated generator: ```bash cd ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/thedotmack npm run bug-report ``` ## Contributing Contributions are welcome! Please: 1. Fork the repository 2. Create a feature branch 3. Make your changes with tests 4. Update documentation 5. Submit a Pull Request against `main` Releases ship from `main` and are published to npm. See [Development Guide](https://docs.claude-mem.ai/development) for contribution workflow. --- ## License Claude-Mem is licensed under the Apache License 2.0. We chose Apache-2.0 because durable agentic memory should be easy to embed in developer tools, local agents, MCP servers, enterprise systems, robotics stacks, and production agent harnesses. See the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for full details. See [docs/license.md](docs/license.md) and [docs/ip-boundary.md](docs/ip-boundary.md) for licensing scope and the open/commercial boundary. --- ## Support - **Documentation**: [docs/](docs/) - **Issues**: [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem/issues) - **Repository**: [github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem) - **Official X Account**: [@Claude_Memory](https://x.com/Claude_Memory) - **Official Discord**: [Join Discord](https://discord.com/invite/J4wttp9vDu) - **Author**: Alex Newman ([@thedotmack](https://github.com/thedotmack)) --- **Built with Claude Agent SDK** | **Works with Claude Code** | **Made with TypeScript** --- ### What About CMEM? CMEM is a token created by a 3rd party but officially embraced by the creator of Claude-Mem (Alex Newman, @thedotmack). The token acts as a community catalyst for growth and a vehicle for bringing CMEM to the developers and knowledge workers that need it most. Official BASE CA: 0x76b1967eec0ccaeb001bbbb2b40dc4badba31ba3

repositories.description: Local voice dictation for mac, windows and linux
repositories.readme:
# Hex

Hex is local voice dictation for Mac, Windows and Linux. Hold a key, speak, and
it pastes.

## How it works

- hold the shortcut, speak, then let go
- Hex transcribes on your device and pastes into whatever app you're in
- the first run downloads a speech model; after that nothing leaves your machine
- experimental features live in Labs, at the bottom of the sidebar

## Downloads

Stable is the current release. Dev is the newest build of `dev` and updates
itself from the dev channel.

| Platform | Stable | Dev |
| --- | --- | --- |
| macOS (Apple silicon) | [DMG](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/macos-arm64-dmg) | [DMG](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/macos-arm64-dmg) |
| Windows x64 | [Installer](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/windows-x64-setup) | [Installer](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/windows-x64-setup) |
| Windows ARM64 | [Installer](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/windows-arm64-setup) | [Installer](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/windows-arm64-setup) |
| Linux x86_64 | [Executable](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-x64) | [Executable](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-x64) |
| Linux x86_64 (Debian, Ubuntu) | [.deb](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-x64-deb) | [.deb](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-x64-deb) |
| Linux x86_64 (Fedora, openSUSE) | [.rpm](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-x64-rpm) | [.rpm](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-x64-rpm) |
| Linux ARM64 | [Executable](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-arm64) | [Executable](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-arm64) |
| Linux ARM64 (Debian, Ubuntu) | [.deb](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-arm64-deb) | [.deb](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-arm64-deb) |
| Linux ARM64 (Fedora, openSUSE) | [.rpm](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/linux-arm64-rpm) | [.rpm](https://anoma.ly/hex/download/dev/linux-arm64-rpm) |

Or install with:

- Homebrew: `brew install --cask anomalyco/tap/hex`
- AUR: `yay -S hex-bin`
- install script (Linux): `curl -fsSL https://anoma.ly/hex/install-linux.sh | sh`
- Nix: `nix profile install github:anomalyco/hex`

More docs are in [`docs/`](docs/README.md).

## Contributing

We don't take pull requests. [Open an issue](https://github.com/anomalyco/hex/issues)
describing the bug or idea, and our agents usually turn it around fast.

MIT licensed.

repositories.name: Orkas
repositories.description: Orkas is an open-source (MIT), local-first AI team for your desktop: a Commander turns your goal into to-dos and coordinates 16 built-in specialist agents plus Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes, with projects, scheduled automations and connectors. Free app for macOS & Windows; built-in models or your own keys.
repositories.readme:
# Orkas **An open-source team of AI agents on your desktop — it turns your goals into finished work and keeps it moving.** Orkas is an open-source (MIT), local-first multi-agent desktop app — an AI assistant that works as a team. Tell the **Commander** what you need: it finishes many tasks on its own, and for bigger work it plans the steps and brings in specialist agents along with the coding and personal agents you already use — **Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent** — to work on it together. Orkas is built to keep a project moving, not just answer one prompt. A **project** holds the goal, rules, memory and files, so every new conversation picks up where the last one left off. **To-dos** split the work between people and agents, **Auto-advance** lets the team take on the next to-do by itself, and **scheduled automations** repeat routine work hourly, daily, weekly or monthly. All your data stays on your computer, and finished work comes back for your review — so you can trust Orkas with the ongoing work of your business. **[⬇ Download Orkas for macOS & Windows](https://orkas.ai/download/?source=gh-orkas&entry_point=github_readme&download=1)** — free, with 500 credits for the built-in Orkas model, so you don't need an API key to start. Prefer your own keys? Claude · OpenAI · Gemini · DeepSeek · Kimi · GLM · Qwen · MiniMax · Doubao, or a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint. ### Recreate a reference video with your own content **VideoStudio** can recreate a viral video's narrative structure, visual style and editing pace using your own product, script and footage. Keep its hook, typography and pacing, replace the content with my product and screen recordings, and show me the breakdown and plan first." Start with a video file the agent can read; social-platform share-link downloading is not built in. Exact camera moves, human performances and frame-by-frame matching are not guaranteed. See the [reference-recreation workflow](./resources/builtin/marketplace/agents/79df9cc89f5f/skills/video-craft/references/reference-recreation.md). --- ## Keep the work moving One task is a good start. Orkas is built for the work that keeps going. - **Projects** — goals & rules, memory and files that every conversation in the project starts from, so you never brief from scratch. - **To-dos and Auto-advance** — every project has a to-do list for people and agents; with Auto-advance on, the team picks up the next item on its own and brings finished work back for your review. - **Scheduled automations** — run any task hourly, daily, weekly or monthly. From v1.9, each automation catches up its most recent missed run within 12 hours when the computer wakes or Orkas starts. - **Connectors** — Gmail, Google Calendar, Sheets and Drive, Notion, Slack, Shopify, Stripe and many more. By default, Orkas asks before it sends, posts or deletes anything. - **Apps** — describe a tool and Orkas builds it as a local app inside the desktop app. In the packaged app, paid plans can also publish it as a web app with a public link. - **Shared projects** *(packaged app)* — invite a teammate or VA, and give each to-do to a person or an agent. > [!NOTE] > Shared projects, cloud sync and web-app publishing are only in the packaged app — the open-source build doesn't support them yet. To use them, **[download Orkas for macOS & Windows](https://orkas.ai/download/?source=gh-orkas&entry_point=github_readme&download=1)** (free, with 500 credits to start). Voice input also works in the source build. Configure an **Orkas API Key** in **Settings → Models**, then click the microphone beside a composer. Allow microphone access when prompted. Audio is sent to Orkas for recognition and uses the key owner’s Orkas credits. Click again to stop, review the text, and send it yourself. If access was denied, enable the microphone in your system settings. --- ## Run Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent together Orkas runs the CLI agents you already have installed as local sessions, next to its own specialists — the coding agents **Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode**, and the personal agents **OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent**. The Commander hands each one the part it's best at and keeps one plan across all of them, so a single chat can fix the bug, review the change and draft the release note. Open-source tools such as HyperFrames plug in the same way. [Using Claude Code and Codex together →](https://orkas.ai/blog/claude-code-codex-together/?source=gh-orkas) --- ## Why Orkas - **A Commander that plans, delegates and does the rest** — it breaks down goals, picks the right agents, skills, connectors and tools, and handles analysis, writing, research and file work itself when no specialist is a better fit. - **Local-first by design** — conversations, files, knowledge bases and custom agents stay on your disk by default. Cloud sync is optional in the packaged app. With your own keys, model calls go straight from your machine to the provider; the built-in Orkas model runs through Orkas's managed model service. - **Any model, switch any time** — the Commander and built-in agents share one model setting: the built-in Orkas model, your own provider, or a local endpoint. External CLI agents keep their own model settings. - **Agents that get better** — each agent keeps private skills and memory. Background reviews examine new activity when the app is idle and can refine self-assessment, reusable methods and learned skills. - **Open source, no black box** — MIT licensed. Read exactly what Orkas and every agent and skill do. > ⭐ If Orkas is useful to you, a star helps more people find the project. --- ## Download | | Packaged app (recommended) | Run from source | | --- | --- | --- | | Platforms | macOS 12+ (Apple Silicon & Intel), Windows 10+ | macOS, Windows, glibc 2.34+ Linux x64/arm64 | | Account | Sign in — 500 free credits | None | | Models | Built-in Orkas model, or your own keys | Your own keys or a local endpoint | | Also includes | Project collaboration, app publishing, cloud sync, and more | — | | Get it | **[Download Orkas](https://orkas.ai/download/?source=gh-orkas&entry_point=github_readme&download=1)** | [Quick start](#quick-start) | The download link detects your system and starts the right installer. --- ## What people use it for - **Marketing content** — launch videos, product pages, posts and newsletters in your voice. [Content writing](https://orkas.ai/use/content-writing/?source=gh-orkas) · [Videos](https://orkas.ai/use/make-videos/?source=gh-orkas) - **Store operations** — weekly sales briefs, review replies, listings and competitor checks. [Developers](https://orkas.ai/use/developers/?source=gh-orkas) - **Build an app** — quote calculators, booking forms, internal tools. [Build apps](https://orkas.ai/use/build-apps/?source=gh-orkas) - **Small teams** — one project for people and agents. [Small teams](https://orkas.ai/use/small-teams/?source=gh-orkas) --- ## How Orkas compares | Tool | What it is | How Orkas differs | | --- | --- | --- | | **Claude Code** | Anthropic's agentic coding tool — in the terminal, IDE, desktop and web, built on Claude models. | Not either-or: Orkas runs Claude Code as one of its agents. Around it, Orkas adds a model-agnostic team for the work beyond code — research, content, video and more — with projects, to-dos and automations that keep it moving. [Orkas vs Claude Code →](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-claude-code/?source=gh-orkas) | | **Codex** | OpenAI's coding agent — in the terminal, your editor and the cloud. | Not either-or: Orkas runs Codex as one of its agents, next to Claude Code and OpenCode. The Commander can hand the coding to Codex and the review to another agent, then cover the non-code half of a release — docs, launch posts and videos. [Orkas vs Codex →](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-codex/?source=gh-orkas) | | **LangChain** | A developer framework/library for building LLM apps and agents — code-first, embedded in your own Python/JS app. | Orkas is a desktop app you direct through chat, not by writing orchestration code. Data stays local by default. | | **CrewAI** | A Python framework for orchestrating role-playing autonomous agents — you define crews and agents in code. | Orkas brings multi-agent orchestration into a desktop app, with projects, to-dos, automations and per-agent self-improvement built in. | | **OpenClaw** | A personal-agent platform with messaging integrations, multi-agent routing and sub-agents. | Orkas provides a desktop workspace for finished deliverables, with built-in specialists and coordination across Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and other CLI agents. OpenClaw can join that workflow as a CLI agent. | | **Hermes-Agent** | Nous Research's self-improving agent — one agent with memory and skills, available as a CLI, a messaging gateway and a desktop app. | Orkas coordinates a team: the Commander directs many specialists and other CLI agents, and Hermes-Agent plugs in as one of them. | **Orkas is for you if** you want a team of agents rather than one assistant, work that keeps moving across days, and your data, keys and agents on your own disk. **Not for you if** you just want a single all-purpose chatbot, or a pure code library to embed in your own app. **Choosing between coding agents?** [Codex vs OpenCode](https://orkas.ai/compare/codex-vs-opencode/?source=gh-orkas) · [Claude Code vs Codex vs OpenCode](https://orkas.ai/compare/claude-code-vs-codex-vs-opencode/?source=gh-orkas) · [Claude Code alternatives](https://orkas.ai/compare/claude-code-alternatives/?source=gh-orkas) **Full side-by-side comparisons →** [vs Claude Code](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-claude-code?source=gh-orkas) · [vs Codex](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-codex?source=gh-orkas) · [vs Cline](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-cline?source=gh-orkas) · [vs LangChain](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-langchain?source=gh-orkas) · [vs ChatGPT](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-chatgpt?source=gh-orkas) · [vs OpenClaw](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-openclaw?source=gh-orkas) · [vs Hermes-Agent](https://orkas.ai/compare/orkas-vs-hermes-agent?source=gh-orkas) --- ## Quick start Want a packaged installer instead? See [Download](#download) above. To run from source — currently the way to run Orkas on Linux: **Requirements**: Node 22.12+ · macOS / Windows 10+ / glibc 2.34+ Linux x64 or arm64. Keep Python 3 and a C/C++ build toolchain available for the uncommon native-module source-build fallback. ```bash git clone https://github.com/Orkas-AI/Orkas.git cd Orkas ./run.sh # macOS / Linux run.cmd # Windows ``` Linux source runs require glibc 2.34+. Alpine and other musl-based distributions are not supported. Local speech transcription downloads and verifies the target-native whisper.cpp runtime and multilingual model during the first source launch. `run.sh` / `run.cmd` installs the locked npm dependency tree and prepares the pinned Python, uv, Node, embedding model (~95 MB), OfficeCLI, FFmpeg, whisper.cpp, and multilingual speech model resources on first launch. Linux startup then verifies the platform-native modules and Whisper runtime under Electron's ABI before opening the app. OCR and Skill-specific Python packages are installed into isolated local environments when those features are first used. First launch creates a workspace under `~/.orkas/` (macOS / Linux) or `:\.orkas\` (Windows). Then open **Settings → AI Providers** to add an API key or OAuth. Native dependency errors: use Node.js 24 LTS (minimum 22.12.0), then run `npm run native:repair` from this checkout. This restores optional packages, repairs SQLite for Electron, prepares bundled Node for isolated image processing, and checks SQL, sqlite-vec and sharp before success. Use `npm run native:check` for a check without installation. See the [native dependency verification script](./scripts/verify-native-dependencies.cjs) for the checks performed. --- ## How it works ### Task routing The Commander handles general work itself and delegates specialist work through three tools: - **`dispatch_to`** runs a named agent and returns its result for continued work. It can wait for the result or run asynchronously and notify the Commander when the task finishes. - **`hand_off_to`** transfers the remaining work to a named agent and ends the current Commander turn. The agent delivers its own reply; an optional continuation lets the Commander resume a broader task afterward. - **`run_worker`** runs an anonymous, isolated sub-task and returns a private result. It does not receive conversation history or a named agent's skills. Named agent tasks and anonymous workers have separate concurrency controls. See the [dispatch implementation](./src/main/features/group_chat/bus.ts) and [execution locks](./src/main/util/locks.ts). ### Context management The runtime budgets context against the selected model's usable input capacity, accounting for prompts, tools and persistent runtime state. Completed dialogue uses a bounded recent-history window; long active tasks use checkpoints to condense earlier process messages while retaining recent work. File reads, file changes and command executions also have structured records that can survive context compaction. See [context budgets](./src/core-agent/src/agent/context-budget.ts), [session history and checkpoints](./src/core-agent/src/agent/session.ts) and [workspace records](./src/core-agent/src/agent/workspace-state.ts). ### Memory and the Library Durable notes keep user preferences, project facts and each agent's reusable knowledge in separate scopes. These notes are distinct from the Library's document index and the stored conversation history. The Library extracts documents into passages and stores a local SQLite vector index. Its embedding model runs on your machine; the `library` tool can list files, search relevant passages and read source content from the global or current-project Library. Earlier conversations are retrieved separately through `chat_history`. See [scoped memory](./src/main/features/memory.ts), [document extraction](./src/main/util/file_to_chunks.ts), [Library tools](./src/main/model/core-agent/kb-tools.ts) and [conversation retrieval](./src/main/model/core-agent/chat-history-tools.ts). ### Execution limits and recovery Session locks and concurrency limits bound parallel work. Tool-round budgets, progress checkpoints, repeated-call checks and phase-aware idle watchdogs help contain runs that stall or repeat work. Named agent tasks can be tracked and cancelled individually; an admitted or queued task is not treated as a completed result. See [actor budgets](./src/main/features/group_chat/actor-budgets.ts), the [agent runtime](./src/core-agent/src/agent/runner.ts) and the [desktop model adapter](./src/main/model/core-agent/client.ts). ### Learning from activity Background reviews examine new agent activity when the app is idle, subject to cooldowns and execution limits. A review may update an agent's self-assessment (`COMPETENCE.md`), reusable methods (`LEARNING_STRATEGIES.md`) or learned skills. Reviews depend on new activity rather than task count, and can conclude that there is nothing worth saving. See the [reflection scheduler](./src/main/features/reflection-orchestrator.ts) and [review prompt](./src/core-agent/src/evolution/metacognition.ts). --- ## FAQ **What is Orkas?** Orkas is an open-source (MIT), local-first multi-agent desktop app. Its Commander turns your goal into to-dos and coordinates 16 built-in specialist agents — plus Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent — to deliver finished files. Not a single chatbot, not a code framework, not a hosted SaaS. **Do I need an API key?** No. The packaged app comes with 500 credits for the built-in Orkas model. After that, buy credits, choose a paid plan or add your own provider keys; provider charges are separate. **Is Orkas a local LLM?** No. Orkas runs on your machine and calls the models you choose — the built-in Orkas model, your own API keys, or a local model endpoint. It orchestrates agents and tools; it is not itself a model. **Can Orkas answer questions from my documents, with citations?** Yes. Add PDFs and documents to your local Library; Orkas can search them and answer with citations to source passages, so you can open the original and check. The index is built on your machine. **Can I use local models like Ollama or LM Studio?** Yes. Open **Account settings → Models → Chat → Add model → Custom**, select **OpenAI-compatible** or **Anthropic-compatible**, and enter the base URL, exact model ID, and API key. Choose the saved model from the task's model control. **Where are my API keys and data stored?** On your disk by default. Your own provider keys are encrypted locally and excluded from cloud sync. With your own keys, model calls go straight from your machine to the provider; the built-in Orkas model uses Orkas's managed service. Optional cloud sync and shared projects in the packaged app store the selected data on Orkas servers. [Security and data handling →](https://orkas.ai/security/?source=gh-orkas) **Does Orkas work offline?** The source build can run fully offline against a local model endpoint. The packaged app needs to sign in, and cloud models need a network connection. **Does it keep working when my computer is off?** No — Orkas runs on your computer, so Auto-advance and automations need the computer awake and Orkas running. From v1.9, each automation catches up its most recent missed run within 12 hours when the computer wakes or Orkas starts. **Can I build and publish apps?** Yes. Local apps that run inside Orkas are free. Publishing a web app to a public link needs a paid plan (Lite 5, Pro 8, Max 15 apps), and published web apps don't include every capability available inside Orkas. **Do I need an Orkas account?** The packaged desktop app asks you to sign in when you first launch it. The source build in this repository has no account layer at all — it boots straight into the app. **Can Orkas drive Claude Code and other CLI agents?** Yes. Orkas can drive five external CLI agents as local subprocesses — the coding agents Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode, plus the personal agents OpenClaw and Hermes-Agent — and onboard open-source projects like HyperFrames, all directed from the same chat. **How is Orkas different from Claude Code / Codex / CrewAI / LangChain?** Claude Code and Codex are coding agents — Orkas runs both as members of its team, so you don't have to choose between them; CrewAI and LangChain are code-first frameworks. Orkas is an open-source desktop app where a Commander coordinates a team of specialist agents and your CLI agents, with any model provider, and keeps data and keys local. See the [full comparisons](https://orkas.ai/compare/?source=gh-orkas). **Which platforms does Orkas support?** macOS 12+ (Apple Silicon and Intel) and Windows 10+ have packaged installers. glibc 2.34+ Linux x64/arm64 runs from source today, with no installer yet. Local speech transcription is supported on Linux through the pinned whisper.cpp runtime prepared on first launch. Alpine and other musl-based distributions are not supported. The source bootstrap needs Node 22.12+; Python 3 and a C/C++ build toolchain are needed only when a native npm package has no compatible prebuilt binary and must be rebuilt locally. **Is Orkas free and open source?** Yes — the app is MIT licensed and free to use. The packaged app includes 500 credits for the built-in Orkas model; paid plans from $11.99/month add monthly credits, cloud sync, more shared projects and app publishing. With your own keys, model usage is billed by your provider; Orkas does not add a markup. [Pricing →](https://orkas.ai/pricing/?source=gh-orkas) --- ## License [MIT](./LICENSE)

# Impeccable The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with `polish` and `bolder`, review with `critique` and `audit`, and catch AI slop before it ships. From your project root: ```bash npx impeccable install ``` Reload your coding tool, then run `/impeccable init` in your agent (`$impeccable init` on Codex). Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto. Full docs live at [impeccable.style/docs](https://impeccable.style/docs). | Without Impeccable | With Impeccable | |---|---| | ![Villa Castagneto built without Impeccable: cream background, a thin serif headline with an italic accent, two pill buttons, and flat vector illustrations in rounded cards](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/raw/main/docs/images/readme-without.webp) | ![Villa Castagneto built with Impeccable: a full-bleed engraved night scene of the villa on its cliff above the sea, a condensed cream and vermilion headline, and a month strip along the bottom](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/raw/main/docs/images/readme-with.webp) | Same model (Fable 5.1), same brief: a fourteen-room family guesthouse on the Ligurian coast. Without Impeccable, it builds the tasteful default: cream page, thin serif, italic accent, pill buttons. With it, the page is built around one picture: the house at night, seen from the water. For a full project, see the [Neo Mirai case study](https://impeccable.style/cases/neo-mirai): a conference site taken from mockup to shipped page. ## Why Inter for everything. Purple-to-blue gradients. Cards nested in cards, gray text on colored backgrounds, a rounded-square icon tile above every heading. Ask an agent for a page with no other guidance and these show up again and again, across models and projects. - **Words for what you want.** "Make it pop" leaves your agent to guess. `/impeccable bolder the pricing cards` loads a playbook written for that one move and points it at one target. - **A reviewer.** `critique` scores the design against usability heuristics and ranks what to fix first. `audit` checks accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behavior, with findings ranked P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish). - **A slop detector.** 62 deterministic rules flag the tells above, plus quality problems like cramped padding and skipped headings. No LLM, no API key. Impeccable is strongest on interfaces that already exist: point it at a page or a component and iterate. It builds new pages too; see [Build something new](https://impeccable.style/docs/new-work) for how to get the most out of that harder mode. To start, pick one component: ``` /impeccable critique the pricing cards ``` ## How it works Run `/impeccable init` once per project. It reads your code, asks only what it can't infer (who the product is for, what it needs to do, the constraints), and writes `PRODUCT.md`. Every later command reads it. Run `/impeccable document` to capture your existing visual system in `DESIGN.md`, so changes stay on-brand. [More on context files](https://impeccable.style/docs/context). Then name a command and a target: ``` /impeccable critique the onboarding flow /impeccable quieter the landing page /impeccable polish settings /impeccable harden checkout ``` Or just describe what you want: `/impeccable redo this hero section`. Narrow targets get better results; a single section reviewed closely beats a whole page at a glance. Pin a command you use often with `/impeccable pin audit` to get `/audit` as its own shortcut. ### 24 commands | | Commands | |---|---| | **Steer** | `bolder` amplifies safe designs · `quieter` tones down loud ones · `distill` removes what the page doesn't need · `colorize` brings color to a gray interface · `typeset` fixes fonts, hierarchy, and sizing · `layout` fixes spacing and rhythm · `animate` adds transitions and interaction feedback · `delight` adds personality · `overdrive` goes for shaders, spring physics, and scroll-driven effects | | **Review** | `critique` is a scored UX review · `audit` is a technical quality report | | **Finish** | `polish` is the final pass before shipping · `harden` covers errors, i18n, overflow, and edge cases · `clarify` rewrites unclear copy · `adapt` handles screen sizes and devices · `optimize` fixes loading and rendering performance · `onboard` designs first-run flows and empty states | | **Iterate live** | `live` lets you pick an element in the browser and cycle through variants · `generate` produces variants of a named element without manual picking | | **Plan and set up** | `shape` plans UX before code · `init` writes `PRODUCT.md` · `document` writes `DESIGN.md` · `extract` pulls repeated patterns into your design system | The 24th, `craft`, is a deprecated alias for a plain build request. Type `/impeccable` alone to see the list in your agent. Each command has its own page: [impeccable.style/docs](https://impeccable.style/docs). On Codex, open `/skills` or type `$impeccable` instead of the slash command. ### Live mode `/impeccable live` opens your running dev server with an overlay. Select an element, pick a direction, and Impeccable hot-swaps variants in place. Accept one and it is written back to your source. It works with Vite, Next, SvelteKit, Astro, Nuxt, and plain HTML. [Iterate in the browser](https://impeccable.style/tutorials/iterate-live). Live mode edits a local checkout only; don't inject it into a deployed site or weaken a production CSP to make it work. Applying copy edits runs your `package.json`'s optional `impeccable:manual-edit-validate` script with your permissions, so review it before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo. ## Three ways to run the detector **In your agent.** The design hook scans every UI file your agent edits and hands the findings back before the agent calls the work done. This is where most slop gets caught: without the hook, the detector only runs when someone remembers to run it. It's available on Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Grok Build, and Hermes Agent, and the installer sets it up. Say yes. [Automatic design checks](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks). **In CI or your terminal.** The CLI needs no agent: ```bash npx impeccable detect src/ # scan a directory npx impeccable detect https://example.com # scan a rendered page (uses your installed Chrome or Edge) npx impeccable detect --json . # machine-readable output npx impeccable detect --github src/ # GitHub Actions annotations npx impeccable detect --list-rules # every rule with its id and description ``` Source files like JSX and TSX get the pattern rules only. Rules that need a rendered page, such as low contrast and tiny text, run when you scan a URL, so point the CLI at your dev server too: `npx impeccable detect http://localhost:5173`. Exit code `2` means findings, `1` means a target couldn't be scanned. To allow your brand font everywhere, run `npx impeccable ignores add-value overused-font Inter --reason "Brand font"`. To turn a rule off for one file, add a comment: ``. [Run a detector scan](https://impeccable.style/docs/detector) · [Configuration and ignores](https://impeccable.style/docs/config). **In your browser.** The [Chrome extension](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/impeccable/bdkgmiklpdmaojlpflclinlofgjfpabf) overlays the same findings on any live page, yours or anyone else's. [Review with a visual overlay](https://impeccable.style/tutorials/critique-with-overlay). ## Installation ```bash npx impeccable install ``` The installer detects your coding tools, asks whether to install for this project or globally, and offers the design hook where your tool supports one. Accept the hook. Reload your tool afterward. `npx impeccable update` refreshes an existing install. For scripts, pass `--providers=claude,codex,cursor` and `--scope=project|global`. Three tools need one more step before the hook runs. In Codex, open `/hooks` and approve the project hook (again after an update that changes it). In Grok Build, run `/hooks-trust` or launch with `--trust`. In Hermes Agent, the hook is a plugin: run `hermes plugins enable impeccable-design-hook` once. [Allow the hook in your harness](https://impeccable.style/docs/hooks#allow-the-hook-in-your-harness). Node is only needed for `npx`. The skill itself runs a self-contained engine binary that ships next to it or downloads once into `~/.impeccable/bin/`.
Claude Code, Copilot, and Grok plugins **Claude Code:** `/plugin marketplace add pbakaus/impeccable`, then open `/plugin` and install Impeccable. **GitHub Copilot in VS Code:** install [Impeccable from the Visual Studio Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=renaissance-geek.impeccable) or run `code --install-extension renaissance-geek.impeccable`. Needs VS Code 1.109.3+, Copilot Chat, and a trusted workspace. It installs the skill without the hook. [Details](docs/VSCODE-EXTENSION.md). **Grok Build:** `grok plugin install pbakaus/impeccable#plugin --trust` installs the skill, agents, and hook.
Git submodule (a pinned version for the whole team) ```bash git submodule add https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable vendor/impeccable npx impeccable link --source=vendor/impeccable --providers=claude,cursor ``` Commit `.gitmodules`, the submodule, and the generated links. Teammates run `git submodule update --init --recursive`. To upgrade, run `git submodule update --remote vendor/impeccable`, rerun the `link` command, and commit. Linking installs skills, not hooks. Existing skill folders stay put unless you pass `--force`.
Manual copy, no Node required Download the ZIP for your tool from [impeccable.style](https://impeccable.style), or clone this repo: each tool's build is committed at the repo root. Copy `skills/impeccable` from the folder below into the same place in your project, or into the global folder. | Tool | Repo folder | Global skills folder | |---|---|---| | Claude Code | `.claude/` | `~/.claude/skills/` | | Cursor | `.cursor/` | | | Codex CLI, Replit Agent | `.agents/` | `~/.agents/skills/` | | Devin | `.devin/` | `${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/devin/skills/` | | GitHub Copilot | `.github/` | | | Gemini CLI | `.gemini/` | | | Google Antigravity | `.agent/` | `~/.gemini/config/skills/` | | OpenCode | `.opencode/` | | | Grok Build | `.grok/` | `~/.grok/skills/` | | Hermes Agent | `.hermes/` | `${HERMES_HOME:-$HOME/.hermes}/skills/` | | DeepSeek Harness | `.dsh/` | `${DSH_HOME:-$HOME/.dsh}/skills/` | | Pi | `.pi/` | | | Qoder | `.qoder/` | `~/.qoder/skills/` | | Rovo Dev | `.rovodev/` | `~/.rovodev/skills/` | | Mistral Vibe | `.vibe/` | `~/.vibe/skills/` | | Trae | `.trae/` | `~/.trae/skills/` | | Trae China | `.trae-cn/` | `~/.trae-cn/skills/` | For example: `mkdir -p your-project/.claude/skills && cp -r .claude/skills/impeccable your-project/.claude/skills/`. Notes: - A manual copy skips the design hook and subagents. Run `npx impeccable install` to get them; it writes each tool's hook pointing at the right skill path. - OpenCode also needs `.opencode/commands/impeccable.md` copied into your project's `.opencode/commands/` to provide `/impeccable`. - Hermes asks you to trust project-local skills once: run `hermes skills trust` from the project root. Global installs need no trust step. - Cursor and Gemini CLI may need Agent Skills enabled in settings. See the [Cursor](https://cursor.com/docs/context/skills) and [Gemini CLI](https://geminicli.com/docs/cli/skills/) skills docs. - Restart Trae after copying. - `impeccable install` and `update` manage a DeepSeek Harness global copy only when `DSH_HOME` is inside your home directory.
## Project files and git Impeccable writes its working files under `.impeccable/`. A few are shared project artifacts and belong in the repo: `config.json`, `live/config.json`, `design.json`, `surfaces/*.md`, and `critique/*.md`. Keep `PRODUCT.md` and `DESIGN.md` in the repo too. The rest is screenshots, caches, and runtime state.
Copy the .gitignore entries ```gitignore # impeccable-ignore-start # Ephemeral output, runtime state, and per-dev overrides. # The **/ prefix covers .impeccable at the repo root or in a nested workspace. # Shared artifacts stay tracked: config.json, live/config.json, # design.json, surfaces/*.md, critique/*.md. **/.impeccable/config.local.json **/.impeccable/hook.cache.json **/.impeccable/hook.pending.json **/.impeccable/*.png **/.impeccable/review/ **/.impeccable/questions/ **/.impeccable/live/server.json **/.impeccable/live/sessions/ **/.impeccable/live/previews/ **/.impeccable/live/annotations/ **/.impeccable/live/cache/ **/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-apply-transaction.json **/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-events.jsonl **/.impeccable/live/manual-edit-evidence/ **/.impeccable/live/pending-manual-edits.json **/.impeccable/live/deferred-svelte-component-accepts.json **/.impeccable/live/*.png # impeccable-ignore-end ```
The folders that hold decision-round state (`.impeccable/questions/`, `.impeccable/mocks/worlds/`) also ignore themselves. A `.gitignore` can't untrack a file git already tracks; if you committed one earlier, run `git rm --cached `. ## Good to know **Build path.** For new landing pages and showcase surfaces, Impeccable can generate a full-fidelity comp first and build to match it (bolder, slower), or build straight in code (leaner, faster). App screens and documents are always built in code. `init` asks once and saves the answer as `buildPath` in `.impeccable/config.json`; the decision page lets you override it for one session. The choice only appears when your harness can generate images. [Image generation](https://impeccable.style/docs/image-generation) · [Configuration](https://impeccable.style/docs/config). **Hooks run outside model approval.** In Claude Code, installed command hooks run even when you deny the model's own commands, so the first edit can download the engine. Review installed hooks before unattended runs, or pass `--settings '{"disableAllHooks": true}'` to turn them off for a run. The installer leaves hook entries it didn't add alone. **Something broken?** `/impeccable doctor` finds stale context files, unused settings, and broken hooks. [Fix setup problems](https://impeccable.style/docs/doctor). **Telemetry.** When a new design starts, the skill fetches a set of visual directions from the impeccable.style catalog. Turning telemetry off doesn't stop that request; it stops the anonymous record of which directions were shown and which one you picked, which is how the catalog learns what works. Your project name, files, code, and `PRODUCT.md` are never sent. Disable telemetry with `npx impeccable telemetry off`, `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`, or `"telemetry": false` in `.impeccable/config.json` for the whole project. The full list of what is sent is on the [privacy page](https://impeccable.style/privacy). ## Community - [Issues](https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/issues) for bugs, questions, and ideas. Outside contributions start with an issue; see [DEVELOP.md](docs/DEVELOP.md). - [Changelog](https://impeccable.style/changelog) for what shipped. - Follow [@pbakaus](https://x.com/pbakaus) for release notes and new rules. ## License Apache 2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). Impeccable started from Anthropic's [frontend-design](https://github.com/anthropics/skills/tree/main/skills/frontend-design) skill. --- Created by [Paul Bakaus](https://www.paulbakaus.com)

# 紫微斗数 · 开源排盘引擎 ### 算法是公开的传统智慧，不应该被锁在围墙里 [![CI](https://github.com/Renhuai123/ziwei-doushu/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Renhuai123/ziwei-doushu/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/code-MIT-blue.svg)](./LICENSE) [![Dataset: CC BY 4.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/dataset-CC%20BY%204.0-green.svg)](./DATASET-LICENSE) **中文** · [English](./README.en.md)
**一、项目理念**：紫微斗数是中国传统命理学的瑰宝，倪海厦老师在《天纪》中系统梳理了正宗的紫微斗数体系。我们希望通过技术手段让更多人接触和学习这门学问。 开源排盘算法和知识库，是因为我们相信：**算法是公开的传统智慧，不应该被锁在围墙里**。真正的价值在于解读的深度、用户体验的打磨、以及持续运营的积累。 **二、项目信息**：基于倪海厦《天纪》教学体系的紫微斗数排盘系统，包含完整排盘算法、四化系统、格局知识库、古籍原文数据，以及一套完整开源的紫微斗数解读数据：**v4.0 解读数据集——67.5 万张命盘 × 13 维 = 877 万段解读，正文约 204 亿字，解压后 56.6 GB**（2026-10-15 发布）。 | 数据集 | 命盘 | 解读段数 | 解压后 | 覆盖年份 | 每张盘解读字数 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | **v4.0 解读数据集**（2026-10-15） | **674,976** | **8,774,688** | **56.6 GB** | **1950–2026**（只含真实日期） | **约 3.0 万字** | | v3.0 样本数据集 | 518,400 | 6,739,200 | 33.1 GB | 1924–1983 | 约 2.1 万字 | | 变化 | +30% | +30% | **+71%** | +17 年 | +44% | v3.0 每张盘解读字数按 2,160 张盘抽样估算，其余数字为全量统计；两版每张盘都是 13 维。 在线体验：[ouranic.cn](https://ouranic.cn/?from=gh-readme)，排盘、AI 解读、命盘历史全部开放。 > **注：关于六亲判断** > > 紫微斗数在六亲（父母、兄弟、子女等）判断上存在一定局限。倪师在《天纪》中指出：“斗数批六亲本来就比较差一点。”（[2上 · 00:25:27](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1KJsLekEfA?p=3&t=1527)）在传统术数中，铁板神数在核对六亲方面有其独特优势（[2上 · 00:03:15](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1KJsLekEfA?p=3&t=195)）；倪师仍以紫微斗数为核心，是因为它能结合地理、环境与人事进行综合判断，形成“上知天文、下知地理、中知人事”的完整体系（[2上 · 00:25:43](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1KJsLekEfA?p=3&t=1543)）。因此，与六亲相关的分析仅供参考；[ouranic.cn](https://ouranic.cn/?from=gh-readme) 上父母、兄弟、子女三个维度也附有同样的说明。 --- ## 目录 | | 章节 | 一句话 | |---|------|--------| | 一 | [本轮更新](#一本轮更新2026-10-15) | 13 维断语按倪师原话与《全书》逐句校正，发布 67.5 万命盘 × 13 维解读数据集 v4.0 | | 二·新 | [13 维解读数据集 v4.0](#二新13-维解读数据集-v402026-10-15) | 2026-10-15 新版断语，67.5 万命盘，按年份下载 | | 二 | [51.8 万命盘样本数据集](#二518-万命盘样本数据集) | 规格、下载、用途、许可 | | 三 | [快速开始](#三快速开始) | 克隆到跑起来 | | 四 | [排盘引擎](#四排盘引擎) | 能做到什么、文件怎么分、古籍数据 | | 五 | [倪师《天纪·紫微斗数》原话](#五倪师天纪紫微斗数原话) | 14 讲 + 2 段补充、1848 条，一图看全，每条可回放 | | 六 | [界面是一份 Demo](#六界面是一份-demo) | 不是线上那套，差距写明 | | 七 | [开源边界](#七开源边界什么不在里面) | 什么开源、什么不开源 | | 八 | [维护节奏与贡献](#八维护节奏与贡献) | 同步节奏、issue / PR 口径 | | 九 | [协议](#九协议) | 代码 MIT / 数据 CC BY 4.0 / 古籍公版 / 倪师原话非商用 | | 十 | [关于与联系](#十关于与联系) | 项目理念、技术栈、联系方式 | --- ## 一、本轮更新（2026-10-15） 本轮跟随网站 2026-10-15 发版（网站内容版本 `ca268829f7a9`）： ![本轮更新总览](./docs/update-20261015.png) **1. 发布 13 维解读数据集 v4.0** —— 674,976 张命盘（公历 1950–2026 年每一个真实日期 × 12 时辰 × 男女）× 13 维 = **8,774,688 段解读**，正文约 204 亿字。解压后 56.6 GB（v3.0 为 33.1 GB，增加 71%），压缩后只有 161 MB，按年份分 77 个文件，可以只下需要的年份，也可以一次下全年份总包。下载见 [Release v4.0-13d](https://github.com/Renhuai123/ziwei-doushu/releases/tag/v4.0-13d)，规格和字段见[第二·新章](#二新13-维解读数据集-v402026-10-15)。发布前 77 个文件逐个解压，与原始数据逐字节比对一致。 **2. 13 维断语按倪师原话与《全书》原文逐句校正**（断语库仍不开源，校正结果体现在 v4.0 数据集里）： - 标着倪师或《全书》却查不到出处的引文，删掉或换成逐字可查的原话；倪师原话注明《天纪》第几集、几分几秒 - 不会发生的四化（如七杀化权、紫微化忌）相关的句子删去；只在某种条件下才成立的断语补上条件 - 「力量强时……落陷时……」这类两头说的句子，改为按命盘只显示成立的那一种 - 健康：哪个脏腑要留意，改按倪师的看法——全盘杀星最集中的那一宫，按它的地支对应脏腑；不再按星的五行推脏器 - 网站知识库「古籍引证」由 244 处增至 405 处，每一处都能在《紫微斗数全书》原文里逐字找到 **3. 排盘引擎同步**（[PR #39](https://github.com/Renhuai123/ziwei-doushu/pull/39)）—— `dst-cn.ts` 新增 `chinaDSTSpan(year)`，查某年中国夏令时起止；`cities.ts` 补全省直辖县级单位与新疆兵团各市的经度（神农架、海南各市县、阿拉尔等），出生地选这些城市时真太阳时校正可用。 **4. 许可** —— [`DATASET-LICENSE`](./DATASET-LICENSE) 适用范围加上 v4.0；写明解读里引用的倪师原话不在数据授权范围内，与第五章倪师原话的 CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 一致。v3.0 样本数据集及其条款不变。 > **2026-10-31 补充**：线上平台更名 **OURANIC**，网址由 metisziwei.com 迁到 **[ouranic.cn](https://ouranic.cn/?from=gh-readme)**（运营主体北京王多鱼科技有限责任公司，京ICP备2026069066号-1）；旧网址会自动跳转，本仓库的代码、数据集与许可都不变。 > **2026-10-27
